content.value_statement: TypeScript test data often needs partial objects without unsafe assertions. This skill guides users through replacing test-only as assertions with @total-typescript/shoehorn helpers.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use shoehorn in TypeScript test files.
Shows the npm install command for @total-typescript/shoehorn.
Converts as Type examples to fromPartial() patterns.
Converts as unknown as Type examples to fromAny() patterns.
Suggests a grep search for test and spec files.
Warns users to avoid shoehorn in production code.
limitations: Focused on TypeScript tests, not production application code.
Does not perform the migration automatically without user direction.
Does not cover every possible type assertion pattern.
Requires project approval before installing a new npm package.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Test Fixtures
use_cases.description: Replace bulky mocked objects with partial test data that keeps TypeScript useful.

use_cases.title: Modernize Type Assertions
use_cases.description: Move common as Type and double assertion patterns to named shoehorn helpers.

use_cases.title: Review Migration Safety
use_cases.description: Check that shoehorn changes remain limited to test files and preserve test intent.

prompt_templates.title: Find Candidate Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Find TypeScript test files that use as assertions and list safe candidates for a shoehorn migration.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate One Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate this test from as Type to fromPartial() and explain any import changes needed.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Wrong Test Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Replace double assertions in this test with fromAny() while preserving the invalid data scenario.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Migration Diff
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this shoehorn migration diff for production usage, changed test meaning, and missing type-check verification.

output_examples.input: A test builds a large request mock only to provide a body id.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends using fromPartial(), adding the shoehorn import, and keeping only the relevant body data.

output_examples.input: A test uses a double assertion to pass intentionally invalid data.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends fromAny(), explains why the invalid value is intentional, and keeps the assertion test readable.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks whether shoehorn belongs in a production file.
output_examples.output: The assistant flags the usage as out of scope and recommends keeping shoehorn limited to test code.

best_practices: Use shoehorn only in test files.
Run type checks after each migration batch.
Keep migrated fixtures minimal and tied to test intent.
anti_patterns: Do not add shoehorn to production code paths.
Do not replace assertions that encode important runtime behavior without review.
Do not hide intentionally invalid data behind unclear helper names.

faq.question: What does this skill migrate?
faq.answer: It migrates TypeScript test assertions from as Type patterns to @total-typescript/shoehorn helpers.

faq.question: Can I use shoehorn in production code?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly limits shoehorn usage to test code.

faq.question: When should I use fromPartial()?
faq.answer: Use fromPartial() when a test needs only part of a larger typed object.

faq.question: When should I use fromAny()?
faq.answer: Use fromAny() when a test intentionally passes invalid data for error handling coverage.

faq.question: Does the skill install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents an npm install command that should be run only with project approval.
